propositions: For a non-Anthropic-family primary model absent from MODEL_LADDER, models_at_or_above returns the entire ladder instead of the primary itself, causing escalation to downgrade the window and cross to a different provider family.

largest_window_tokens returns MODEL_LADDER[-1][1] for an unlocated primary instead of the ladder minimum, overstating the available window and causing P8 to under-block, resulting in silent truncation instead of actionable decomposition feedback.

The prerequisite-coverage escalation path inherits the same defect through models_at_or_above, causing the single-criterion retry step to be skipped and the run to jump to claude-haiku-4-5 instead of staying on the operator's configured model.

For a truthy-but-unlocated primary, models_at_or_above should return [model] to preserve the single-criterion retry step before escalation climbing, and largest_window_tokens should return min(w for _, w in MODEL_LADDER) to conservatively prevent under-blocking.

Three assertions in test_model_class_ladder.py pinned the pre-fix behavior and must be updated to assert the corrected behavior: models_at_or_above returning the primary alone and largest_window_tokens returning the ladder minimum for unlocated models.
